correctness.rationale: For a smooth \(\ell_p^2\) unit vector \(x=(a,b)\), Birkhoff--James orthogonality fixes the tangent direction \(y\) up to scale. The functional characterization of Dragomir approximate orthogonality reduces the best reverse threshold to the norm-one functional annihilating \(x\), producing the scalar factor \(c_p(u)\) in RESULT.md. For \(p=3\) and \(p=3/2\) the dual formulas coincide. With \(w=\sqrt{u(1-u)}\), the reciprocal cube is \((1+2w)(1-2w^2)\); its derivative has the unique interior maximum at \((\sqrt7-1)/6\), and substitution gives \((17+7\sqrt7)/27\). The stated \(\varepsilon_D\) follows exactly. An independent 200001-point scan of \(w\in[0,1/2]\) located the same unique maximizer and reproduced \(0.4087812568462646\), while the radical identity was checked symbolically/numerically.

value.rationale: The parameter is the sharp global quantitative version of a standard asymmetry question for Birkhoff--James orthogonality. Computing it exactly for a canonical smooth conjugate pair of non-Hilbert planes, and showing the extremum is genuinely interior rather than axial or diagonal, gives a meaningful benchmark for the general qualitative theorem.
residual_risks: The result treats only one Hölder-dual pair and does not give \(\varepsilon_D(\ell_p^2)\) for general \(p\).

final_claim: For the real Hölder-dual Banach planes \(\ell_3^2\) and \(\ell_{3/2}^2\), the optimal global Dragomir approximate-symmetry parameter for Birkhoff--James orthogonality is \[\varepsilon_D=\sqrt{1-\left(\frac{27}{17+7\sqrt7}\right)^{2/3}}=0.408781256846\ldots,\] and the worst reverse-orthogonality configuration is attained at the unique interior ratio corresponding to \(w=(\sqrt7-1)/6\).
limitations: Real two-dimensional \(\ell_p\) spaces only for \(p=3\) and \(p=3/2\).
The result concerns Dragomir's approximate orthogonality, not the distinct Chmieliński approximate relation.
